title: Accelerating Viz Pipelines Using Near-Data Computing: An Early Experience
problem: Traditional visualization pipelines transfer entire data arrays from storage to client nodes for processing, creating unnecessary data transfer overhead when visualization filters only operate on small subsets of the data.
motivation: Reducing data transfer volumes in visualization pipelines improves performance and efficiency for scientific computing and large-scale simulations.
method: The visualization pipeline is divided into pre-filters executing near data on storage nodes using computational storage and smart NICs, and post-filters on client nodes. Pre-filters preprocess and subset data near storage before transfer based on downstream pipeline needs, while post-filters complete processing on the client side. Evaluation uses two real-world simulation datasets.
key_novelty: Applying near-data processing to visualization pipelines by partitioning pre-filters to storage nodes and post-filters to clients, significantly reducing network data transfer requirements.
contributions: Split-pipeline architecture with pre-filters executing near-data and post-filters on client
2.8× reduction in visualization data load times compared to traditional full-transfer approaches
11.9× speedup when combined with data compression techniques
Evaluation and validation on real-world simulation datasets
limitations: Not discussed; paper described as early experience with limited evaluation scope
